items.title: Nelson–Aalen, Kaplan–Meier, and Greenwood estimators
items.statement: For right-censored observations (U_i,δ_i), define the subject counting and at-risk processes, pooled risk/event counts, the Nelson–Aalen estimator, Kaplan–Meier product limit, and Greenwood variance estimate with explicit endpoint, tie, zero-risk, and positive-denominator conventions.
items.strategy: Give the finite-sample statistic definitions under the event-observation and estimator interfaces; distinguish the discrete-support cumulative event hazard from the continuous cumulative hazard and label Greenwood as first-order asymptotic variance estimation.

items.title: Finite-support risk-set proportion limits
items.statement: For IID right-censored subjects with T independent of C, finite event support a_1<...<a_m, and positive event and censoring survival through a_j, the pooled at-risk proportion at a_j converges in probability to P(T≥a_j)P(C≥a_j)>0 and the event proportion converges to P(T=a_j)P(C≥a_j); their ratio converges to q_j=P(T=a_j|T≥a_j).
items.strategy: Apply Chebyshev's inequality to the bounded IID risk and observed-event indicators at each of finitely many support points, then use independent censoring and positivity to take the ratio.

items.title: Finite-support consistency of Nelson–Aalen and Kaplan–Meier
items.statement: For IID right-censored subjects with T independent of C and finite event-time support, at every fixed horizon t through which P(T>t)>0 and P(C≥t)>0, the Kaplan–Meier estimator converges in probability to S(t)=P(T>t), while the Nelson–Aalen estimator converges to the discrete cumulative hazard sum Σ_{a_j≤t}q_j, where q_j=P(T=a_j|T≥a_j).
items.strategy: Use the proved event-to-risk ratio limits at the finitely many support points and induct on ordered event times to obtain the product limit and the discrete cumulative-hazard sum; explicitly retain the censoring-support boundary.

items.title: Uniform convergence of the empirical right-censoring risk set
items.statement: For IID observed event/censoring pairs, the empirical at-risk fraction n^{-1}Σ_i 1{U_i≥u} converges uniformly in probability on every compact horizon to s_0(u)=P(U_i≥u), and the expected squared uniform error tends to zero.
items.strategy: Use finite partitions of the one-dimensional distribution of U, Chebyshev convergence at partition points, monotonicity between points, and bounded convergence in probability.

items.title: Pointwise influence limit and Greenwood variance consistency
items.statement: For IID right-censored subjects with continuous event-time law, independent censoring, a continuous-hazard compensator contract, positive event and censoring survival on [0,t], and ∫_0^t λ(u)/s_0(u)du<∞, prove the pointwise expansion √n(Ŝ_n(t)−S(t))=n^{-1/2}Σ_i φ_i(t)+o_P(1), where φ_i(t)=−S(t)∫_0^t s_0(u)^{-1}dM_i(u), s_0(u)=E[Y_i(u)]>0; prove the terminal normal limit and that n times a zero extension of Greenwood's formula converges to Var(φ_i(t)). No process-level convergence or confidence bands are asserted.
items.strategy: Prove uniform risk-set convergence and square integrability, replace the random Nelson–Aalen denominator by s_0 in L² using the counting-process isometry, apply the IID terminal influence theorem, bound the log-product remainder, use the pointwise delta method, and prove Greenwood consistency by compensator decomposition.

items.title: A hand Kaplan–Meier calculation and loss of tail support
items.statement: For four right-censored observations with failures at 1 and 2 and two censorings at 3, compute the pooled risk counts, Nelson–Aalen estimate, Kaplan–Meier estimate, and Greenwood estimate through time 3; show that a fixed censoring horizon makes survival beyond 3 nonidentifiable by exhibiting two event-time laws with the same observed-data law but different tails.
items.strategy: Compute each failure increment from its risk set, substitute into the three estimator definitions, then compare the induced observed records under two latent event-time laws that agree through the censoring horizon and differ after it.
